failure_summary.description: Cached results were ignored, redundantly searched, or left unchanged when the user added a filterable criterion or referred to a proposed place.
Agents imported the unavailable tools module despite the skill requiring direct calls to injected functions.
The round-trip request was represented as one outbound search instead of separate outbound and return searches.
A new hotel search result was not saved to the cache.

patch.reasoning: Cache misuse is the most common actionable pattern: agents returned no-ops or repeated searches instead of applying new criteria to compatible results. Make retrieval and filtering steps explicit, and clarify that contextual questions can refer to the assistant's proposed place. Tool-call and persistence rules already exist, as does the separate-leg round-trip rule, so duplicating them is unwarranted.

edits.target: - On each turn, consider the full conversation and cached result summaries. Reuse cached results only when their domain and subject match the request. If the user adds criteria, retrieve the closest compatible result, apply the matching filter, and save the updated result. Do not filter unrelated results; search for a requested entity or category that the cached results do not cover. Avoid retrieving unrelated results or repeating constraints in filters that were already applied. Save each newly generated search or transformation result under a unique cache key. Use “No planning needed” only when cached results already satisfy every current request.
edits.content: - On each turn, compare every current request and criterion with the full conversation and compatible cached result summaries. Reuse results only when their domain and subject match. A summary is metadata, not a result object: when a compatible cached result needs a new criterion, call `get_results_from_cache(key="...")`, assign the returned result, pass it as `prior_results` to the matching `filter_*` tool, then assign and save the filtered result under a unique key. Apply new criteria to every affected compatible result set, including each affected flight leg. Do not re-search a domain when compatible cached results already cover it; search only when the cache lacks a compatible result for the requested subject or category. Do not filter unrelated results or repeat constraints already satisfied. Save every newly generated search or transformation under a unique cache key. Use “No planning needed” only when compatible cached results satisfy every current request and criterion.

edits.target: - Resolve brief affirmations such as “yes” against the immediately preceding assistant question or proposal, and carry forward the proposed entity or category as stated.
edits.content: - Resolve contextual follow-ups such as “what’s there?” or “tell me about that” against the immediately preceding proposal. When the proposal names a place or category relevant to an existing result set, treat it as a new criterion: retrieve the compatible result, apply the matching filter using the proposed value, and save the updated result rather than treating the follow-up as a no-op.
